title.en: The Lord Bless You and Keep You

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
Peter Lutkin was the first dean of Northwestern University's School of Music, from 1895 until 1928.
Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 3, then sing it back.
Hear line 4, then sing it back.
Now lines 3 and 4 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 5, then sing it back.
Hear line 6, then sing it back.
Now lines 5 and 6 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 8, then sing it back.
Hear line 9, then sing it back.
Hear line 10, then sing it back.
Now lines 8 to 10 joined, with the guide.
The Lord bless you start to end, with the guide.
Sevenfold Amen start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of The Lord Bless You and Keep You in Sing, with the other parts playing.
The Methodist Hymnal of 1905, which Lutkin helped edit, prints this blessing with a plain two-chord Amen in place of his sevenfold one.

source.en: The Methodist Hymnal (New York: Eaton & Mains, 1905), No. 748, p. 532, read from the scan; Wikipedia, "Peter Lutkin" (he co-edited a Methodist hymnal)
